elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction over all disputes under this Agreement is exclusive.
elements.evidence: Although the clause generally provides for exclusive jurisdiction, it permits either party to seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction. The preferred position contains no such exception.

elements.element: The designated forum includes the state courts in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly designates state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The designated forum includes the federal courts in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly designates federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any of the permitted fallback laws.

elements.element: The designated courts correspond to the selected fallback law: courts in Delaware for Delaware law, courts in California for California law, or courts in London for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause designates New York County courts rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or London courts.

result.reason: The New York governing-law provision and specified New York County state and federal courts match the preferred position, but the added temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out materially qualifies the required exclusive jurisdiction. The redline therefore does not fully satisfy the preferred position, and its New York selections do not satisfy the independently assessed fallback. The carve-out was unnecessary to reach the preferred position, so the redline is not minimal. The language is otherwise coherent and does not disturb unrelated terms.
